name: Umm Al-Jimāl
description: Umm Al-Jimāl, whose name means "Mother of Camels," is a ruined village of dark basalt stone in northern Jordan, about 17 km east of Mafraq. Houses, churches and re-used Roman military buildings still stand above ground, built between the 5th and 8th centuries. Inscriptions in five languages, from Greek to Arabic, and the remains of an ancient water-catching system reveal how its farmers and herders lived.
